370	/**
371	 * One file of the released tree.
372	 * @param root - the repository the program delivered into.
373	 * @param revision - the merged head, or undefined for a program that released none.
374	 * @param path - the path to read out of that tree.
375	 * @returns the file's text, or an empty string when the tree does not carry it.
376	 */
377	function released(root: string, revision: string | undefined, path: string): string {
378	  if (revision === undefined) return ''
379	  try {
380	    return execFileSync('git', ['show', `${revision}:${path}`], { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf8' })
381	  } catch {
382	    // A failed integration releases no tree to read; the ledger states why, and
383	    // the empty text is what a reader of this line gets.
384	    return ''
385	  }
386	}
387	
388	/**
389	 * The files the released tree carries.
390	 * @param root - the repository the program delivered into.
391	 * @param report - the report whose merged revision is read.
392	 * @returns every path of the merged tree, sorted, or an empty list for a program that released none.
393	 */
394	function deliverable(root: string, report: ProgramReport): string[] {
395	  if (report.mergedRevision === undefined) return []
396	  const listed = execFileSync('git', ['ls-tree', '-r', '--name-only', report.mergedRevision], { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf8' })
397	  return listed.split('\n').filter(line => line !== '').sort()
398	}
399	
400	/**
401	 * Run the committed examiner over the integration worktree once more, outside
402	 * the program, so the recorded run carries a verdict this driver observed
403	 * rather than one it read out of a certificate.
404	 * @param workspace - the integration worktree.
405	 * @returns the examiner's exit code and what it wrote.
406	 */
407	function examine(workspace: string): VerifierLine {
408	  if (!existsSync(join(workspace, 'verify-safety-report.mjs'))) return { exitCode: -1, output: 'no integration worktree' }
409	  try {
410	    const output = execFileSync(process.execPath, ['verify-safety-report.mjs', '--report'], { cwd: workspace, encoding: 'utf8', stdio: 'pipe' })
411	    return { exitCode: 0, output }
412	  } catch (error) {
413	    const failed = error as { status?: number; stdout?: string; stderr?: string }
414	    return { exitCode: failed.status ?? -1, output: `${failed.stdout ?? ''}${failed.stderr ?? ''}` }
415	  }
416	}
417	
418	// The report repository has to exist before the program plugin validates its
419	// workspaceRoot, so it is minted — and the target locked — before the
420	// composition loads.
421	const lock = lockTarget(target)
422	ensureRepository(reportRepository, lock)
423	
424	const ctx = await boot('code-safety-program', resolveConfigPath(configPath, undefined))
425	try {
426	  // Loader siblings mount concurrently; the program mounts presets and reads
427	  // persisted sessions, so the driver drives only the settled application.
428	  await ctx.get('loader')?.await()
429	  const programs = ctx.get('programs')
430	  const persistence = ctx.get('sessionPersistence')
431	  if (programs === undefined || persistence === undefined) throw new Error('code-safety driver requires the programs and session persistence services')
432	  const denials: DenialLine[] = []
433	  ctx.on('session/event', (session, event) => {
434	    if (event.type === 'read-barrier/denied') {
435	      denials.push({ sessionId: session.id, capability: event.data.capability, displayPath: event.data.displayPath })
436	    }
437	  }, { global: true })
438	  const spec = programSpec(lock)
439	  await sign(ctx, spec, reportRepository)
440	  const started = Date.now()
441	  const report = await programs.start(spec)
442	  const observed = await readRoot(persistence)
443	  const integration = join(reportRepository, report.programId, INTEGRATION_KEY)
444	  process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify({
445	    type: 'result',
446	    report,
447	    target: { root: lock.root, files: Object.keys(lock.files).length, sha256: lock.sha256 },
448	    elapsedSeconds: Math.round((Date.now() - started) / 1000),
449	    denials,
450	    deliverable: deliverable(reportRepository, report),
451	    safetyReport: released(reportRepository, report.mergedRevision, 'SAFETY-REPORT.md'),
452	    findings: released(reportRepository, report.mergedRevision, 'findings.json'),
453	    verifier: examine(integration),
454	    ...observed,
455	  })}\n`)
456	} finally {
457	  await ctx.fiber.dispose()
458	}

1	# Test-only composition: one program of the Daliesk Village that reviews a
2	# target tree for code-safety defects — six departments, one git worktree and
3	# session each, an integration over the merged head, and a ledger in the
4	# program's own session.
5	#
6	# This file is the keyless half: the departments run on the scripted `cli-mock`
7	# route below, against the committed `sample-target/`, so the whole workflow
8	# executes with no key and no network. `overlays/claude-code.cordis.yml` is the
9	# same composition with the operator's Claude Code route in its place, which is
10	# the one a real review boots.
11	- id: code-safety-llm
12	  name: './code-safety-llm.ts'
13	
14	# Managed child-process groups for the bash executor (spawn/kill/output plumbing).
15	- id: subprocess
16	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local'
17	
18	- id: bash
19	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-local'
20	
21	- id: fs
22	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-local'
23	  config:
24	    cwd: !!js process.cwd()
25	
26	# The barrier the program denies its integration session the department
27	# worktrees with; the fs gate is what refuses the read in the operation that
28	# opens paths. It does not make the target tree read-only — no capability here
29	# does — which is why the base commit carries `target.json` and the committed
30	# examiner re-hashes every locked file on every run.
31	- id: read-barrier
32	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier'
33	
34	- id: fs-read-barrier
35	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier'
36	
37	- id: tool-fs
38	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs'
39	
40	# A department reads a tree it did not write, so `glob` and `grep` are how it
41	# finds what to open. An over-cap page is sampled across top-level entries
42	# rather than taking the newest files: a review's first pass wants breadth.
43	- id: tool-fs-search
44	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs-search'
45	  config:
46	    sampleOverCapGlobResults: true

48	- id: goal
49	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal'
50	  config:
51	    defaultMaxGoalRounds: 11
52	
53	# Composed beside the program, which disarms every goal it creates: a department
54	# an operator resumes by hand is driven by this row instead.
55	- id: goal-round-driver
56	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal-round-driver'
57	
58	- id: verification
59	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'
60	  config:
61	    maxChecks: 32
62	    maxTextChars: 4096
63	
64	# The roster's root is absolute: the smoke runs in an isolated temporary cwd, so
65	# the presets beside this file are reachable only through the path the driver
66	# exports. `integrating` is the default because the integration session is
67	# created with no preset of its own.
68	- id: agent-presets
69	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets'
70	  config:
71	    default: integrating
72	    roots:
73	      - path: !!js process.env.DSH_CODE_SAFETY_PRESETS
74	        trust: system
75	    includeUserRoot: false
76	
77	# The route every department session is created with. The overlay replaces this
78	# entry, and only this entry, to put a product model in the departments' place.
79	- id: agent-default-model
80	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-default-model'
81	  config:
82	    provider: cli-mock
83	    model: cli-mock
84	
85	# Village rule: a composition that runs unattended sessions carries a session
86	# budget. The caps are far out of reach of the scripted route, so no department
87	# breaches them before its own `budget/caps` record tightens them.
88	- id: budget-policy
89	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy'
90	  config:
91	    maxTotalTokens: 6000000
92	    maxWallMs: 3600000
93	
94	- id: agent-spine
95	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-spine-demo'
96	  config:
97	    persona: 'You review code you did not write for security defects, on your own branch, and you report only what you have read.'
98	    workspaceContext: false
99	
100	# The ledger and every department log outlive the process, so a restarted run
101	# reconciles from the same root the first pass wrote.
102	- id: persistence
103	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl'
104	  config:
105	    root: !!js process.env.DSH_TEST_SESSION_ROOT ?? './.sessions'
106	    compression: none
107	
108	- id: checkpoint-policy
109	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-checkpoint-policy'
110	
111	# The two signatures the program's `requireSignoff` reads are recorded on the
112	# program session by the driver, through this service, before `start` opens it.
113	- id: signoff
114	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-signoff'
115	  config:
116	    maxEvidence: 8
117	    maxEvidenceRefChars: 512
118	
119	- id: program
120	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-program'
121	  config:
122	    workspaceRoot: !!js process.env.DSH_CODE_SAFETY_REPORT_REPO
123	    requireSignoff: true
124	    # One department at a time keeps the keyless ledger's order a property of
125	    # the spec rather than of the host's scheduling; the overlay raises it,
126	    # because six departments reading one tree have nothing to serialize on.
127	    maxConcurrentGoals: 1
128	    # A department spends one round reading and committing. The integration
129	    # spends its first round discovering that no report exists yet, because its
130	    # checks run before its first turn.
131	    maxGoalRounds: 4
132	    branchPrefix: safety
133	    # The examiner's failures are the only instruction a department gets between
134	    # attempts, so the evidence bound has to carry several of them whole.
135	    evidenceMaxChars: 4096

# AGENTS.md — Examples

Runnable harness compositions. `examples/` is one workspace member and the module-resolution root for runnable and test Cordis configs; it is not a build target. [package.json](package.json) declares the packages loaded by those configs, while each leaf's private `package.json` remains metadata only.

Extract reusable logic into `packages/`, where per-file coverage and README gates apply. Examples keep only `cordis.yml` wiring, demo artifacts, and e2e/snapshot scenarios; app package bins own boot glue.

## E2E smokes

Each example has both:

- **Keyless:** boot the real `cordis.yml` through the Loader, drive it, and assert output and clean exit. Catches invalid Loader exports that hand-mounted tests miss ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **With-key:** send a live-model prompt and verify external state, not the model's claim. Self-skip without `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`; see [testing.md](../docs/testing.md).

Keyless process smokes use `@deepseek-ai/dsh-loader-smoke` for Loader launch resolution; terminal tests wrap that launch in a pseudo-terminal. Tests supply paths, environment, input, and assertions. Every checked-in test Cordis config lives under its corresponding `examples/<agent>/` leaf. Map a package-owned config to `examples/<agent>/tests/fixtures/<group>/<package>/cordis.yml`, keep its driver and assertions package-local, and declare every package it names in both root `tsconfig.json` references and `examples/package.json`.

Do not inventory example tests here; the `tests/` trees and root scripts are authoritative.

In `cordis.yml`, comment only non-obvious wiring, load-order consequences, replay, security boundaries, and configuration scope. Do not narrate visible entries; use [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for required coverage and editorial judgment.

See [the root AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) for repo-wide conventions and [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md) for the design.

1	# The code-safety program with the operator's own Claude Code installation as
2	# the route every session is driven through: the real review, and the only file
3	# that differs from the keyless composition beside it.
4	#
5	# `implementer` stays `route`, so the program drives each department turn by
6	# turn through the LLM seam and the department's own session holds every step it
7	# took. The spec digest covers the implementer but not the route, so a keyless
8	# and a real run over the same target are the same program id.
9	#
10	# One model serves every session: the frozen spec carries no per-goal model and
11	# `agent-default-model` is process-wide, so a run cannot staff its departments
12	# and its integration differently.
13	- id: base
14	  name: '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-include'
15	  config:
16	    path: ../cordis.yml
17	    patches:
18	      # The scripted adapter is the keyless half's whole reason to exist; a real
19	      # run composes no mock route at all.
20	      - id: code-safety-llm
21	        disabled: true
22	      - insert:
23	          - id: llm-claude-code
24	            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-claude-code'
25	            config:
26	              provider: claude-code
27	              models:
28	                - id: sonnet
29	                  name: Claude Code sonnet
30	                  productModel: sonnet
31	                  contextWindow: 200000
32	                - id: opus
33	                  name: Claude Code opus
34	                  productModel: opus
35	                  contextWindow: 200000
36	              effort: high
37	      # The code-safety knowledge pack as the session's only skill root, found
38	      # from the repository root above `baseUrl` the way the bench's craft-skills
39	      # overlay finds its own. A tree that carries no pack resolves to no root at
40	      # all rather than to an empty directory, so the pack is optional without
41	      # the composition pretending it is there.
42	      - id: agent-spine
43	        name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-spine-demo'
44	        config:
45	          persona: 'You review code you did not write for security defects, on your own branch, and you report only what you have read.'
46	          workspaceContext: false
47	          skills:
48	            filesystem:
49	              includeDefaultRoots: false
50	              watch: false
51	              customSkillDirs: !!js |
52	                (() => {
53	                  const { fileURLToPath } = process.getBuiltinModule('node:url')
54	                  const { existsSync } = process.getBuiltinModule('node:fs')
55	                  const { dirname, join } = process.getBuiltinModule('node:path')
56	                  const named = process.env.DSH_CODE_SAFETY_SKILLS

1	/**
2	 * Keyless REAL-composition coverage for a program that reviews code: one boot
3	 * of `fixtures/program-code-safety/cordis.yml` over a temporary report
4	 * repository, reading the fixture's committed `sample-target/`. Six security
5	 * departments each certify their own findings on their own branch, and the
6	 * integration merges them and certifies the merged report against the examiner
7	 * committed before any of them started.
8	 *
9	 * The scripted implementer reports the findings pinned in the fixture's
10	 * `code-safety-llm.ts`, reading each `snippet` out of the target at stream
11	 * time. What this proves is the workflow and the examiner — that the target
12	 * stays read-only, that every finding resolves at the line it cites, that a
13	 * finding which does not is refused, and that the committed examiner decides
14	 * the release — not what a model finds. The overlay under the fixture's
15	 * `overlays/` is the same program driven on the operator's Claude Code route,
16	 * which is what answers that question.
17	 */
18	
19	import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process'
20	import { mkdtemp, readFile, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
21	import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
22	import { join } from 'node:path'
23	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
24	import { afterAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
25	import { LOADER_SMOKE_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS, runLoaderSmoke } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-loader-smoke'
26	import { INTEGRATION_KEY } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-program'
27	import type { ProgramEnd, ProgramGoalRecord, ProgramIntegrationRecord, ProgramStart } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-program'
28	
29	const fixtureDir = fileURLToPath(new URL('./fixtures/program-code-safety/', import.meta.url))
30	const binScript = join(fixtureDir, 'driver.ts')
31	const configPath = join(fixtureDir, 'cordis.yml')
32	const sampleTarget = join(fixtureDir, 'sample-target')
33	const repoTsconfig = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../tsconfig.json', import.meta.url))
34	
35	/** Six departments, an integration and seven examiner runs outrun the default window. */
36	const PHASE_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000
37	
38	/** The six departments of the program, in the order the spec declares them. */
39	const DEPARTMENTS = ['secrets', 'injection', 'access', 'data', 'dependencies', 'platform']
40	
41	/** Every finding id the merged `findings.json` carries, sorted. */
42	const FINDING_IDS = [
43	  'access-admin-users-unauthenticated',
44	  'access-self-promotion',
45	  'data-cleartext-transport',
46	  'data-md5-password',
47	  'data-pii-in-logs',
48	  'dependencies-lodash-prototype-pollution',
49	  'dependencies-marked-redos',
50	  'injection-eval-request-body',
51	  'injection-mongo-where',
52	  'injection-sql-concatenation',
53	  'platform-insecure-session-cookie',
54	  'platform-stack-trace-to-client',
55	  'platform-wildcard-cors-with-credentials',
56	  'secrets-api-token',
57	  'secrets-database-password',
58	  'secrets-session-secret',
59	]
60	
61	/** Findings per severity the merged report states, which the examiner cross-checks against the union. */
62	const SEVERITY_COUNTS: Record<string, number> = { critical: 5, high: 9, medium: 2, low: 0, info: 0 }
63	
64	/** Base-commit files no department and no integration may change. */
65	const IMMUTABLE = ['REPORTING.md', 'verify-safety-report.mjs', 'target.json']
66	
67	interface RunLine {
68	  attempt: number
69	  verdict: string
70	  results: { checkId: string; status: string }[]
71	}
72	
73	interface MemberLine {
74	  sessionId: string
75	  programId: string
76	  key: string
77	  certified: boolean
78	  caps: unknown
79	  runs: RunLine[]
80	  directives: string[]
81	}
82	
83	interface Finding {
84	  id: string
85	  cwe: string
86	  severity: string
87	  confidence: string
88	  file: string
89	  line: number
90	  snippet: string
91	}
92	
93	interface DriverResult {
94	  type: string
95	  report: {
96	    programId: string
97	    sessionId: string
98	    outcome?: string
99	    mergedRevision?: string
100	    goals: { key: string; status: string; revision?: string; tree?: string }[]
101	  }
102	  target: { root: string; files: number; sha256: string }
103	  elapsedSeconds: number
104	  ledgers: { sessionId: string; events: { type: string; data: unknown }[]; signoffs: string[] }[]
105	  members: MemberLine[]
106	  denials: { sessionId: string; capability: string; displayPath: string }[]
107	  deliverable: string[]
108	  safetyReport: string
109	  findings: string
110	  verifier: { exitCode: number; output: string }
111	}
112	
113	const roots: string[] = []
114	
115	afterAll(async () => {
116	  await Promise.all(roots.splice(0).map(root => rm(root, { recursive: true, force: true })))
117	})
118	
119	/** The statuses one ledger recorded for one goal key, in log order. */
120	function statuses(events: { type: string; data: unknown }[], key: string): string[] {
121	  return events
122	    .filter(event => event.type === 'program/goal' && (event.data as ProgramGoalRecord).key === key)
123	    .map(event => (event.data as ProgramGoalRecord).status)
124	}
125	
126	/** The member line of one goal key, which every key of a released program has. */
127	function memberOf(observed: DriverResult, key: string): MemberLine {
128	  const found = observed.members.find(member => member.programId === observed.report.programId && member.key === key)
129	  expect(found, `no member session for ${key}`).toBeDefined()
130	  return found as MemberLine
131	}
132	
133	/** Run the committed examiner in one worktree, returning its exit code and output. */
134	function examine(workspace: string, args: readonly string[]): { exitCode: number; output: string } {
135	  try {
136	    const output = execFileSync(process.execPath, ['verify-safety-report.mjs', ...args], { cwd: workspace, encoding: 'utf8', stdio: 'pipe' })
137	    return { exitCode: 0, output }
138	  } catch (error) {
139	    const failed = error as { status?: number; stdout?: string; stderr?: string }
140	    return { exitCode: failed.status ?? -1, output: `${failed.stdout ?? ''}${failed.stderr ?? ''}` }
141	  }
142	}
143	
144	describe('a program that reviews code through a real cordis.yml', () => {
145	  it('certifies six departments over verified findings and releases one examined report', async () => {
146	    const sessions = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'code-safety-sessions-'))
147	    const repository = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'code-safety-repo-'))
148	    roots.push(sessions, repository)
149	
150	    const { stdout, stderr } = await runLoaderSmoke({
151	      label: 'program-code-safety',
152	      tempDirPrefix: 'program-code-safety-e2e-',
153	      binScript,
154	      libBinScript: binScript,
155	      configPath,
156	      binArgs: [configPath],
157	      tsconfigPath: repoTsconfig,
158	      processTimeoutMs: PHASE_TIMEOUT_MS,
159	      env: {
160	        DSH_TEST_SESSION_ROOT: sessions,
161	        DSH_CODE_SAFETY_REPORT_REPO: repository,
162	        DSH_CODE_SAFETY_TARGET: sampleTarget,
163	      },
164	    })
165	    expect(stderr).toBe('')
166	    const observed = JSON.parse(stdout.trimEnd().split('\n').at(-1) ?? '') as DriverResult
167	    expect(observed.type).toBe('result')
168	
169	    expect(observed.report.outcome).toBe('released')
170	    expect(observed.report.goals.map(goal => [goal.key, goal.status]))
171	      .toEqual(DEPARTMENTS.map(key => [key, 'merged']))
172	
173	    const ledger = observed.ledgers.find(candidate => candidate.sessionId === observed.report.programId)
174	    expect(ledger, 'no ledger for the program').toBeDefined()
175	    const events = ledger?.events ?? []
176	    const opened = events[0]?.data as ProgramStart
177	    expect(events[0]?.type).toBe('program/start')
178	    expect(opened.specSha256).toBe(observed.report.programId.replace('program-', ''))
179	    expect(opened.baseRevision).toBe('base')
180	    // The spec is frozen before anything runs, and the route the departments
181	    // are driven on is not part of it: the overlay's real run is this same
182	    // program over a different target.
183	    expect(opened.implementer).toEqual({ kind: 'route' })
184	    expect(ledger?.signoffs).toEqual(['spec-freeze', 'release'])
185	
186	    // No department depends on another: six analysts read one tree.
187	    for (const key of DEPARTMENTS) {
188	      expect(statuses(events, key), key).toEqual(['pending', 'running', 'certified', 'merged'])
189	    }
190	    const integrations = events
191	      .filter(event => event.type === 'program/integration')
192	      .map(event => event.data as ProgramIntegrationRecord)
193	    expect(integrations.map(record => record.status)).toEqual(['running', 'certified'])
194	    const closing = events.at(-1)?.data as ProgramEnd
195	    expect(events.at(-1)?.type).toBe('program/end')
196	    expect(closing.outcome).toBe('released')
197	
198	    // Every department was certified over a commit of its own, and the ledger
199	    // records both the revision and the tree that certificate covers.
200	    const certified = observed.report.goals.map(goal => goal.revision)
201	    expect(certified.every(revision => /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/.test(revision ?? ''))).toBe(true)
202	    expect(new Set(certified).size).toBe(DEPARTMENTS.length)
203	    expect(observed.report.goals.every(goal => /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/.test(goal.tree ?? ''))).toBe(true)
204	    expect(certified).not.toContain(observed.report.mergedRevision)
205	
206	    // Each department runs under the caps the spec gave it and is certified on
207	    // exactly two checks: the examiner over its own findings, and the rule that
208	    // it wrote its own section of the report.
209	    for (const key of DEPARTMENTS) {
210	      const department = memberOf(observed, key)
211	      expect(department.certified, key).toBe(true)
212	      expect(department.caps).toEqual({ maxTotalTokens: 4_000_000, maxWallMs: 2_400_000 })
213	      expect(department.runs.at(-1)?.results.map(result => [result.checkId, result.status]))
214	        .toEqual([[`${key}-findings`, 'pass'], [`${key}-section`, 'pass']])
215	    }
216	    // The `platform` department leaves its first attempt uncommitted: the
217	    // program refuses to measure that worktree, names why, and certifies the
218	    // attempt that commits.
219	    expect(memberOf(observed, 'platform').directives)
220	      .toEqual(['the worktree carries work that no commit on this branch carries'])
221	    expect(observed.members.filter(member => member.programId === observed.report.programId).map(member => member.key).sort())
222	      .toEqual([INTEGRATION_KEY, ...DEPARTMENTS].sort())
223	
224	    // The integration is handed no objective: its first attempt discovers that
225	    // the merge carries no report, and its second one writes it.
226	    const integration = memberOf(observed, INTEGRATION_KEY)
227	    expect(integration.runs.map(run => run.verdict)).toEqual(['failed', 'passed'])
228	    expect(integration.runs.at(-1)?.results.map(result => [result.checkId, result.status]))
229	      .toEqual([['safety-report', 'pass'], ['gate-1', 'pass'], ['gate-2', 'pass']])
230	    expect(observed.denials).toEqual([])
231	    expect(integrations.at(-1)?.denied).toEqual([join(repository, observed.report.programId)])
232	
233	    // The committed examiner is what releases the program, and the driver ran
234	    // it once more over the released worktree.
235	    expect(observed.verifier.exitCode).toBe(0)
236	    expect(observed.verifier.output).toContain('SAFETY-REPORT.md and findings.json verified')
237	
238	    // The union carries every department's findings, each resolving at the line
239	    // it cites in the tree the base commit locked.
240	    const findings = JSON.parse(observed.findings) as Finding[]
241	    expect(findings.map(finding => finding.id).sort()).toEqual(FINDING_IDS)

1	# How this program reports what it found
2	
3	This worktree is the **report repository**. The code under review is the **target tree**, which is somewhere else on this host: `target.json` beside this file states its absolute path, the files it covers, and the SHA-256 the whole tree locks to.
4	
5	The target is read-only for every session of this program. `verify-safety-report.mjs` re-hashes every locked file on every run, so a target a department edited fails the program instead of releasing a report about a tree that no longer exists.
6	
7	## This file and the skills
8	
9	When the deployment mounts the code-safety knowledge pack, its `review-method`, `severity-and-evidence` and `report-template` skills own the craft: how to read a codebase, how to score a severity, what evidence has to name, and how the report reads. Follow them.
10	
11	This file owns what `verify-safety-report.mjs` mechanically decides, and it is binding wherever the two differ in form. There is one such place and it is stated below: the counts each summary carries are written as `- <severity>: <count>` lines so the examiner can compare them with the union, which is the machine-readable form of the skill's "counts per severity".
12	
13	## What a department delivers
14	
15	Two files, both committed on the department's own branch:
16	
17	- `findings/<department>.json` — a JSON array of findings, `[]` when the department found nothing.
18	- `report/<department>.md` — the department's own prose: what it looked at, what it found, and what it did not reach.
19	
20	Nothing else. Do not write `SAFETY-REPORT.md`, `findings.json`, `target.json` or `verify-safety-report.mjs`: the first two are the integration's, and the last two are the examiner.
21	
22	## The evidence rule
23	
24	A finding without a file and a line is not a finding. Quote the exact line you cite; `verify-safety-report.mjs` compares your `snippet` with the target's own text at that line, ignoring only whitespace, and refuses the whole file when they differ.
25	
26	Prefer three findings you have read the code for over twelve a pattern matched. `confidence` is what you actually know: `confirmed` when you read the sink, the source and the path between them; `likely` when the sink is dangerous and the source is plausibly attacker-controlled; `possible` when the pattern is there and the reachability is not established.
27	
28	## The finding
29	
30	```json
31	{
32	  "id": "secrets-cookie-secret",
33	  "cwe": "CWE-798",
34	  "owasp": "A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures",
35	  "severity": "high",
36	  "confidence": "confirmed",
37	  "title": "Session cookie secret is hard-coded in the committed configuration",
38	  "file": "config/env/all.js",
39	  "line": 8,
40	  "snippet": "cookieSecret: \"session_cookie_secret_key_here\",",
41	  "evidence": "The value is a literal in a committed file and is the secret express-session is configured with.",
42	  "impact": "Anyone with the repository can forge a session cookie and authenticate as any user.",
43	  "fix": "Read the secret from the environment and rotate the committed value.",
44	  "references": ["https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html"]
45	}
46	```
47	
48	| Field | Rule |
49	| --- | --- |
50	| `id` | letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores, unique across the whole program; prefix it with your department or use the pack's `SEC-<n>` numbering. |
51	| `cwe` | `CWE-<number>`. |
52	| `owasp` | the OWASP Top 10 category, named. |
53	| `severity` | `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low` or `info`. |
54	| `confidence` | `confirmed`, `likely` or `possible`. |
55	| `title` | one line a reader can act on. |
56	| `file` | path relative to the target root, exactly as `target.json` lists it. |
57	| `line` | 1-based line in that file. |
58	| `endLine` | optional last line when the finding spans several; `snippet` then quotes all of them. |
59	| `snippet` | the target's own text at those lines, verbatim. |
60	| `evidence` | why this line is the vulnerability, naming what you read. |
61	| `impact` | what an attacker gets. |
62	| `fix` | what to change. |
63	| `references` | array of URLs or identifiers; may be empty. |
64	
65	## Checking your own work before you commit
66	
67	```sh
68	node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings findings/<department>.json
69	```
70	
71	That is the same command your goal is measured by. Run it, fix what it names, then commit everything — work left uncommitted is not delivered and is not measured.
72	
73	## What the integration delivers
74	
75	The integration merges every department branch and then writes two files of its own.
76	
77	`findings.json` is the union of every `findings/<department>.json`, deduplicated by `file` + `line` + `cwe`, keeping the entry with the higher `confidence`. Before writing it, ask the examiner which findings do not hold:
78	
79	```sh

81	```
82	
83	Every id that command prints is dropped from `findings.json` and named under `## What was not covered`, with the reason the examiner gave. Dropping one silently fails the report: `--report` refuses a union that omits an id no section discloses.
84	
85	`SAFETY-REPORT.md` carries exactly these sections, in this order:
86	
87	```markdown

89	
90	<deux paragraphes en français : ce qui a été examiné, ce qui a été trouvé, ce que cela implique>
91	
92	- critical: 0
93	- high: 0
94	- medium: 0
95	- low: 0
96	- info: 0
97	
98	## Executive summary
99	
100	<the same in English>
101	
102	- critical: 0
103	- high: 0
104	- medium: 0
105	- low: 0
106	- info: 0
107	
108	## Scope and method
109	
110	<the target, its locked file count, which departments ran, which tools ran — the scanner, the advisory source — and which files were actually read>
111	
112	## Findings
113	
114	### critical
115	
116	- `<id>` — <title> (`<file>:<line>`, <cwe>, <confidence>) — <impact, then fix>
117	
118	### high
119	
120	...
121	
122	## What was not covered
123	
124	- <a department, a file kind, a class of vulnerability, or a check that did not run, and why>
125	- <every dropped finding id, with the examiner's reason>
126	
127	## Certificate
128	
129	Verified findings: <count>
130	Target tree: <the sha256 from target.json>
131	
132	<one sentence on what was checked mechanically: that every finding resolves to a real file and line in the locked tree, that every id is unique, and that no two findings share file, line and CWE>
133	
134	This review does not certify the absence of vulnerabilities; it certifies only that each listed finding was mechanically verified to exist at the cited line, over the files listed in "Scope and method".
135	```

Every finding id in `findings.json` is cited in `## Findings`. Every `<file>:<line>` written anywhere in the report must resolve in the target, so write a path you did not read as prose rather than as a citation.

1	#!/usr/bin/env node
2	// Mechanical examiner of a code-safety report. It is in the report
3	// repository's base commit, so no department can change what measures it.
4	//
5	//   node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings <path>  one department's findings
6	//   node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings <path> --list-invalid
7	//   node verify-safety-report.mjs --report           the merged report
8	//
9	// `--findings` decides one findings file against the target tree. Adding
10	// `--list-invalid` turns the same decision into a report: the failing ids go to
11	// stdout, one per line, and the exit code is 0, which is how the integration
12	// learns which findings to drop and disclose.
13	//
14	// `--report` decides SAFETY-REPORT.md and findings.json together, including the
15	// disclosure rule: every id any `findings/<department>.json` carries and
16	// findings.json does not must be named under `## What was not covered`.
17	//
18	// Exit 0 only when every rule holds; otherwise every failure is printed to
19	// stderr, one per line, and the exit code is 1. Node built-ins only, because
20	// this runs in a worktree that installs nothing.
21	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
22	import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
23	import { basename, join, relative, resolve } from 'node:path'
24	
25	/** Severities a finding may claim, most severe first. */
26	const SEVERITIES = ['critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low', 'info']
27	
28	/** How sure a finding's author is that the cited code is exploitable as described. */
29	const CONFIDENCES = ['confirmed', 'likely', 'possible']
30	
31	/** Sections SAFETY-REPORT.md carries, in this order. */
32	const SECTIONS = [
33	  '## Résumé exécutif',
34	  '## Executive summary',
35	  '## Scope and method',
36	  '## Findings',
37	  '## What was not covered',
38	  '## Certificate',
39	]
40	
41	/** The claim the certificate must make verbatim, and the only claim this review supports. */
42	const HONESTY = 'This review does not certify the absence of vulnerabilities; it certifies only that each listed finding was mechanically verified to exist at the cited line, over the files listed in "Scope and method".'
43	
44	/** Claims no coverage this review can state would support. */
45	const OVERCLAIMS = /\bno vulnerabilities\b|\bfree of vulnerabilities\b|\b(?:is|are|was|were) secure\b|\bsafe to deploy\b|\bproven secure\b|\bfully audited\b/i
46	
47	/** Text a report still carrying its template is refused for. */
48	const PLACEHOLDER = /\bTODO\b|\bTBD\b|\bFIXME\b|lorem ipsum|<placeholder>|PLACEHOLDER/i
49	
50	/** String fields every finding states in prose. */
51	const PROSE_FIELDS = ['title', 'evidence', 'impact', 'fix']
52	
53	/** How a file's text is compared with a finding's quoted snippet. */
54	const normalize = (text) => text.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim()
55	
56	/** Lowercase hex SHA-256 of one buffer or string. */
57	const sha256 = (content) => createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex')
58	
59	/**
60	 * Every file under one directory, relative and sorted, skipping the excluded names.
61	 * @param {string} root directory to walk
62	 * @param {string[]} exclude directory basenames never descended into
63	 * @returns {string[]} relative POSIX-ish paths, sorted
64	 */
65	function walk(root, exclude) {
66	  const found = []
67	  const descend = (directory) => {
68	    for (const entry of readdirSync(directory, { withFileTypes: true }).sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))) {
69	      const path = join(directory, entry.name)
70	      if (entry.isDirectory()) {
71	        if (!exclude.includes(entry.name)) descend(path)
72	      } else if (entry.isFile()) found.push(relative(root, path))
73	    }
74	  }
75	  descend(root)
76	  return found.sort()
77	}
78	
79	/** One target tree as the lock and the verifier both read it: the files, their digests, and their text. */
80	class Target {
81	  /**
82	   * @param {string} reportRoot the report repository the lock is committed in
83	   * @param {string[]} failures collector every rule appends to
84	   */
85	  constructor(reportRoot, failures) {
86	    this.failures = failures
87	    this.root = undefined
88	    this.files = new Map()
89	    this.lines = new Map()
90	    const lockPath = join(reportRoot, 'target.json')
91	    if (!existsSync(lockPath)) {
92	      failures.push('target.json is missing from this worktree; the base commit carries the lock of the tree under review')
93	      return
94	    }
95	    const lock = JSON.parse(readFileSync(lockPath, 'utf8'))
96	    this.root = lock.root
97	    this.exclude = lock.exclude ?? []
98	    this.digest = lock.sha256
99	    for (const [path, hash] of Object.entries(lock.files)) this.files.set(path, hash)
100	    this.checkTree()
101	  }
102	
103	  /**
104	   * Refuse a target that changed since the base commit locked it: a finding
105	   * cites a line of the tree this program was asked to review, and a tree a
106	   * department edited is no longer that tree.
107	   */
108	  checkTree() {
109	    if (!existsSync(this.root)) {
110	      this.failures.push(`the target tree ${this.root} is not on this host, so no citation can be resolved`)
111	      this.root = undefined
112	      return
113	    }
114	    const present = walk(this.root, this.exclude)
115	    for (const path of present) {
116	      if (!this.files.has(path)) this.failures.push(`the target tree gained ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
117	    }
118	    for (const [path, hash] of this.files) {
119	      if (!present.includes(path)) {
120	        this.failures.push(`the target tree lost ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
121	        continue
122	      }
123	      if (sha256(readFileSync(join(this.root, path))) !== hash) {
124	        this.failures.push(`the target tree's ${path} changed since the base commit locked it; the target is read-only for this program`)
125	      }
126	    }
127	  }
128	
129	  /**
130	   * The lines of one target file.
131	   * @param {string} path path relative to the target root
132	   * @returns {string[] | undefined} the file's lines, or undefined when it is not in the locked tree
133	   */
134	  linesOf(path) {
135	    if (this.root === undefined || !this.files.has(path)) return undefined
136	    if (!this.lines.has(path)) this.lines.set(path, readFileSync(join(this.root, path), 'utf8').split('\n'))
137	    return this.lines.get(path)
138	  }
139	
140	  /**
141	   * Whether one `file:line` citation resolves in the locked tree.
142	   * @param {string} path path relative to the target root
143	   * @param {number} line 1-based line number
144	   * @returns {boolean} whether the file is under review and holds that line
145	   */
146	  resolves(path, line) {
147	    const lines = this.linesOf(path)
148	    return lines !== undefined && Number.isInteger(line) && line >= 1 && line <= lines.length
149	  }
150	}
151	
152	/**
153	 * Decide one finding against the target tree.
154	 * @param {unknown} finding one entry of a findings file
155	 * @param {number} index its position, named when the entry has no usable id
156	 * @param {Target} target the locked tree the finding cites
157	 * @param {Set<string>} seen ids already used in this file
158	 * @returns {string[]} every rule this finding broke, empty when it holds
159	 */
160	function checkFinding(finding, index, target, seen) {
161	  const failures = []
162	  if (finding === null || typeof finding !== 'object' || Array.isArray(finding)) {
163	    return [`finding #${index + 1} is not a JSON object`]
164	  }
165	  const id = finding.id
166	  const name = typeof id === 'string' && id !== '' ? id : `#${index + 1}`
167	  const fail = (rule) => void failures.push(`${name}: ${rule}`)
168	  // Letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`: wide enough for both the `SEC-001`
169	  // numbering the knowledge pack's schema uses and a department-prefixed name.
170	  if (typeof id !== 'string' || !/^[A-Za-z0-9][\w.-]*$/.test(id)) fail('id must be letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores')
171	  else if (seen.has(id)) fail('id is used twice in this file')
172	  else seen.add(id)
173	  if (typeof finding.cwe !== 'string' || !/^CWE-\d+$/.test(finding.cwe)) fail('cwe must match CWE-<number>')
174	  if (typeof finding.owasp !== 'string' || finding.owasp.trim() === '') fail('owasp must name the category')
175	  if (!SEVERITIES.includes(finding.severity)) fail(`severity must be one of ${SEVERITIES.join(', ')}`)
176	  if (!CONFIDENCES.includes(finding.confidence)) fail(`confidence must be one of ${CONFIDENCES.join(', ')}`)
177	  for (const field of PROSE_FIELDS) {
178	    if (typeof finding[field] !== 'string' || finding[field].trim() === '') fail(`${field} must be a non-empty string`)
179	  }
180	  if (!Array.isArray(finding.references) || finding.references.some(reference => typeof reference !== 'string')) {
181	    fail('references must be an array of strings')
182	  }
183	  const { file, line, endLine, snippet } = finding
184	  if (typeof file !== 'string' || file === '' || file.startsWith('/') || file.split('/').includes('..')) {
185	    fail('file must be a path relative to the target root')
186	    return failures
187	  }
188	  const lines = target.linesOf(file)
189	  if (lines === undefined) {
190	    fail(`file ${file} is not in the tree under review`)
191	    return failures
192	  }
193	  if (!Number.isInteger(line) || line < 1 || line > lines.length) {
194	    fail(`line ${JSON.stringify(line)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
195	    return failures
196	  }
197	  const last = endLine === undefined ? line : endLine
198	  if (!Number.isInteger(last) || last < line || last > lines.length) {
199	    fail(`endLine ${JSON.stringify(endLine)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
200	    return failures
201	  }
202	  if (typeof snippet !== 'string' || snippet.trim() === '') {
203	    fail('snippet must quote the cited line')
204	    return failures
205	  }
206	  const quoted = normalize(lines.slice(line - 1, last).join('\n'))
207	  if (normalize(snippet) !== quoted) {
208	    fail(`snippet does not match ${file}:${line}, which reads ${JSON.stringify(quoted.slice(0, 160))}`)
209	  }
210	  return failures
211	}
212	
213	/**
214	 * Read one findings file.
215	 * @param {string} path the file to read
216	 * @param {string[]} failures collector a malformed file is reported on
217	 * @returns {unknown[]} the entries, empty when the file is missing or malformed
218	 */
219	function readFindings(path, failures) {
220	  if (!existsSync(path)) {
221	    failures.push(`${path} is missing`)
222	    return []
223	  }
224	  let parsed
225	  try {
226	    parsed = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, 'utf8'))
227	  } catch (error) {
228	    failures.push(`${path} is not JSON: ${error.message}`)
229	    return []
230	  }
231	  if (!Array.isArray(parsed)) {
232	    failures.push(`${path} must be a JSON array of findings`)
233	    return []
234	  }
235	  return parsed
236	}
237	
238	/**
239	 * Decide one findings file on its own.
240	 * @param {string} path the findings file
241	 * @param {Target} target the locked tree it cites
242	 * @returns {{ failures: string[], invalid: string[], findings: unknown[] }} the broken rules, the ids that broke them, and the entries
243	 */
244	function checkFindingsFile(path, target) {
245	  const failures = []
246	  const findings = readFindings(path, failures)
247	  const invalid = []
248	  const seen = new Set()
249	  findings.forEach((finding, index) => {
250	    const broken = checkFinding(finding, index, target, seen)
251	    if (broken.length === 0) return
252	    failures.push(...broken.map(rule => `${basename(path)}: ${rule}`))
253	    invalid.push(typeof finding?.id === 'string' ? finding.id : `#${index + 1}`)
254	  })
255	  return { failures, invalid, findings }
256	}
257	
258	/**
259	 * The body of one section of the report.
260	 * @param {string} text the whole report
261	 * @param {string} heading the section heading, including its `##`
262	 * @returns {string} the text between this heading and the next one, empty when absent
263	 */
264	function section(text, heading) {
265	  const start = text.indexOf(`${heading}\n`)
266	  if (start === -1) return ''
267	  const body = text.slice(start + heading.length + 1)
268	  const next = body.search(/^## /m)
269	  return next === -1 ? body : body.slice(0, next)
270	}
271	
272	/**
273	 * Decide SAFETY-REPORT.md, findings.json and the disclosure of what was dropped.
274	 * @param {string} root the report repository
275	 * @param {Target} target the locked tree the report cites
276	 * @returns {string[]} every rule the report broke
277	 */
278	function checkReport(root, target) {
279	  const reportPath = join(root, 'SAFETY-REPORT.md')
280	  if (!existsSync(reportPath)) {
281	    return [`SAFETY-REPORT.md is missing; REPORTING.md in this worktree states the sections it carries: ${SECTIONS.join(', ')}`]
282	  }
283	  const text = readFileSync(reportPath, 'utf8')
284	  const failures = []
285	  let previous = -1
286	  for (const heading of SECTIONS) {
287	    const at = text.indexOf(`${heading}\n`)
288	    if (at === -1) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md has no section ${JSON.stringify(heading)}`)
289	    else if (at < previous) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md has ${JSON.stringify(heading)} out of order; the order is ${SECTIONS.join(' then ')}`)
290	    else previous = at
291	  }
292	  const placeholder = PLACEHOLDER.exec(text)
293	  if (placeholder !== null) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md still carries placeholder text: ${JSON.stringify(placeholder[0])}`)
294	  const overclaim = OVERCLAIMS.exec(text)
295	  if (overclaim !== null) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md claims more than this review supports: ${JSON.stringify(overclaim[0])}`)
296	
297	  const union = checkFindingsFile(join(root, 'findings.json'), target)
298	  failures.push(...union.failures)
299	  const findings = union.findings.filter(finding => typeof finding?.id === 'string')
300	
301	  const keys = new Set()
302	  for (const finding of findings) {
303	    const key = `${finding.file}:${finding.line}:${finding.cwe}`
304	    if (keys.has(key)) failures.push(`findings.json states ${key} twice; the union is deduplicated by file, line and cwe`)
305	    keys.add(key)
306	  }
307	
308	  const listed = section(text, '## Findings')
309	  for (const finding of findings) {
310	    if (!listed.includes(finding.id)) failures.push(`the Findings section does not cite ${finding.id}`)
311	  }
312	  // The lookbehind keeps a URL's `host:port` out of the citation vocabulary:
313	  // the host is preceded by a slash, so no citation ever starts there.
314	  for (const [, path, line] of text.matchAll(/(?<![\w/.\-])([\w.-]+(?:\/[\w.-]+)*\.\w+):(\d+)\b/g)) {
315	    if (!target.resolves(path, Number(line))) failures.push(`the citation ${path}:${line} does not resolve in the tree under review`)
316	  }
317	
318	  const counts = Object.fromEntries(SEVERITIES.map(severity => [severity, findings.filter(finding => finding.severity === severity).length]))
319	  for (const heading of ['## Résumé exécutif', '## Executive summary']) {
320	    const body = section(text, heading)
321	    for (const severity of SEVERITIES) {
322	      const stated = new RegExp(`^- ${severity}: (\\d+)$`, 'm').exec(body)
323	      if (stated === null) failures.push(`${heading} does not state a "- ${severity}: <count>" line`)
324	      else if (Number(stated[1]) !== counts[severity]) {
325	        failures.push(`${heading} states ${severity}: ${stated[1]}, and findings.json holds ${counts[severity]}`)
326	      }
327	    }
328	  }
329	
330	  const uncovered = section(text, '## What was not covered')
331	  const department = join(root, 'findings')
332	  const dropped = []
333	  if (existsSync(department)) {
334	    for (const entry of readdirSync(department).sort()) {
335	      if (!entry.endsWith('.json')) continue
336	      for (const finding of readFindings(join(department, entry), failures)) {
337	        if (typeof finding?.id !== 'string') continue
338	        if (!findings.some(kept => kept.id === finding.id)) dropped.push(finding.id)
339	      }
340	    }
341	  }
342	  for (const id of dropped) {
343	    if (!uncovered.includes(id)) {
344	      failures.push(`${id} was dropped from findings.json and is not disclosed under "## What was not covered"`)
345	    }
346	  }
347	
348	  const certificate = section(text, '## Certificate')
349	  if (!certificate.includes(HONESTY)) failures.push(`the Certificate must state, verbatim: ${JSON.stringify(HONESTY)}`)
350	  const stated = /^Verified findings: (\d+)$/m.exec(certificate)
351	  if (stated === null) failures.push('the Certificate does not state a "Verified findings: <count>" line')
352	  else if (Number(stated[1]) !== findings.length) failures.push(`the Certificate states ${stated[1]} verified findings, and findings.json holds ${findings.length}`)
353	  const tree = /^Target tree: ([0-9a-f]{64})$/m.exec(certificate)
354	  if (tree === null) failures.push('the Certificate does not state a "Target tree: <sha256>" line')
355	  else if (tree[1] !== target.digest) failures.push(`the Certificate states target tree ${tree[1]}, and target.json locks ${target.digest}`)
356	  return failures
357	}
358	
359	const argv = process.argv.slice(2)
360	const root = resolve(process.cwd())
361	const listInvalid = argv.includes('--list-invalid')
362	const findingsAt = argv.indexOf('--findings')
363	const failures = []
364	const target = new Target(root, failures)
365	
366	if (findingsAt !== -1) {
367	  const path = argv[findingsAt + 1]
368	  if (path === undefined) {
369	    console.error('FAIL --findings needs a path')
370	    process.exit(1)
371	  }
372	  const checked = checkFindingsFile(resolve(root, path), target)
373	  if (listInvalid) {
374	    for (const id of checked.invalid) console.log(id)
375	    process.exit(0)
376	  }
377	  failures.push(...checked.failures)
378	  // A department that found nothing states `[]` and says so in its report
379	  // section: requiring a finding would buy one by inventing it.
380	  if (failures.length === 0) console.log(`ok: ${checked.findings.length} findings verified against ${target.root}`)
381	} else if (argv.includes('--report')) {
382	  failures.push(...checkReport(root, target))
383	  if (failures.length === 0) console.log(`ok: SAFETY-REPORT.md and findings.json verified against ${target.root}`)
384	} else {
385	  console.error('usage: verify-safety-report.mjs --findings <path> [--list-invalid] | --report')
386	  process.exit(1)
387	}
388	
389	if (failures.length > 0) {
390	  for (const failure of failures) console.error(`FAIL ${failure}`)
391	  process.exit(1)
392	}
393	process.exit(0)

content.content:
packages/preset/agent-presets/src/authoring.ts
packages/preset/agent-presets/src/discovery.ts
